analysis.data_caveats: The "conflict" and "political_violence_targeting_civilians" events are almost entirely GDELT-coded diplomatic/cooperation stories (e.g. Spain honoring Moroccan counterterrorism officials, Morocco-Gaza references, a US-Morocco arms contract, a French murder-suspect arrest) rather than actual kinetic violence, and several entries reference unrelated countries (Mexico, Indiana, US Marine) — these appear to be mis-tagged/noisy CAMEO codes, not verified Morocco-based unrest. There is only 1 protest_civil_unrest event and it is the same Spain-related GDELT item, so genuine civil-unrest signal is essentially absent in this window. Investment data is dominated by pre-2025 entries (2019-2024), so it does not capture the most recent 12-18 months of financing activity.
analysis.economic_analysis: IMF data show Morocco's real GDP growth holding steady at 4.9% for both 2025 and 2026, with inflation low and stable (0.8% in 2025 rising modestly to 1.3% in 2026, IMF). World Bank figures corroborate the growth trend (4.6% GDP growth in 2025) and show unemployment easing from 9.1% (2024) to 9.0% (2025), though IMF's unemployment series is notably higher (13.0% in 2025, 12.2% in 2026 projected) — a methodological discrepancy between sources worth flagging. Government debt remains elevated but on a slightly improving trajectory (67.1% of GDP in 2025 to 65.8% in 2026, IMF), while the current account deficit is projected to widen from -2.1%/-2.5% (2025, IMF/WorldBank) to -3.1% of GDP (2026, IMF).
analysis.investment_analysis: Financing activity spans multiple large infrastructure and energy projects: the Noor Midelt CSP-PV solar plant ($837.5M, active as of 2020, WorldBankPPI), Tanger Med II Port Container Terminal 3 ($212.5M, 2021, WorldBankPPI), Taza Onshore Wind ($201.2M, 2020, WorldBankPPI), Safi/Jorf Desalination Plants ($188.0M, 2024, WorldBankPPI), and Koudia Al Baida wind farm repowering ($131.1M, 2022, WorldBankPPI) — indicating sustained private-sector-led investment in energy and water infrastructure per the World Bank PPI Database (39 entries tied to "Private sector"). Chinese financing is a distinct and recurring channel, mostly health-sector grants and COVID-19 assistance (Sinopharm vaccine donations worth $9.0M in March 2021, CDB anti-epidemic supplies $1.1M in May 2020) alongside a large unspecified RMB 100 million grant via ETCA ($14.6M, 2019, AidData) — Chinese financiers (Ministry of Commerce, Chinese Embassy, China Eximbank, CDB) collectively appear in 60 of the tracked investment entries. US development finance is comparatively modest, with DFC direct lending to Ifria Cold Chain Development ($9.3M, FY2023) and technical assistance to Sharaka Capital Fund ($3.5M, FY2024). ICT/digital infrastructure also features, including the MEDUSA Submarine Cable ($71.8M, 2023) and N+ONE African data center portfolio ($45.0M, 2023, WorldBankPPI).
key_relationships: - Government of Morocco is the top-linked actor (n=46, investment category), reflecting its central role as recipient/counterparty across World Bank PPI, DFC, and Chinese-financed projects.

- Chinese state institutions (Unspecified Chinese Government Institution n=33, China Ministry of Commerce n=16, Chinese Embassy n=6, China Eximbank n=5, CDB n=4) collectively represent the largest identifiable foreign financier bloc, concentrated in health-sector grants (AidData records, 2020-2021).

- US-Morocco security/defense cooperation appears in GDELT items: a $398 million AMRAAM missile contract naming Morocco as a partner (Morocco World News, 2026-06-30) and consultations tied to the Moroccan frigate Mohammed VI's visit to New York (Northafricapost, 2026-07-02).

- Spain-Morocco counterterrorism cooperation was highlighted on 2026-07-02 (Morocco World News), the same date as the sole recorded protest_civil_unrest event, both drawn from the identical source article.

- DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) financing is narrowly targeted at cold-chain logistics (Ifria Cold Chain, Agadir, FY2023) and capital markets technical assistance (Sharaka Capital Fund, FY2024).
risk_flags: - Apparent data-quality/mis-tagging issue: several "conflict" and "political_violence_targeting_civilians" events reference actors unrelated to Morocco (Mexico, Indiana, US Marine, 2026-06-30, GDELT), suggesting noise in the automated event-coding pipeline rather than substantive security incidents.
- Divergent unemployment figures between IMF (12.2%-13.0%, 2025-2026) and World Bank (9.0%-9.1%, 2024-2025) reduce confidence in a single precise labor-market read.
- Widening current account deficit projected for 2026 (-3.1% of GDP, IMF) versus -2.1% in 2025, a trend worth monitoring alongside still-high government debt (65.8% of GDP, 2026, IMF).

- Heavy reliance on a small number of large, multi-year-old flagship projects (Noor Midelt 2020, Tanger Med II 2021) with no comparably large new commitments recorded after 2024 in this dataset, which may reflect a data lag rather than an actual slowdown.
analysis.security_analysis: The nine "conflict" entries in this dataset are largely artifacts of GDELT's CAMEO coding applied to diplomatic and cooperation news stories — e.g., "Spain honors Moroccan security officials, hails counterterrorism cooperation" (Morocco World News, 2026-07-02) and a Hoceima police arrest of a French murder suspect (Morocco World News, 2026-06-30) — rather than reports of active armed conflict inside Morocco. Two entries are explicitly about unrelated countries (Mexico/Indiana/US Marine, 2026-06-30, GDELT via Yahoo News), indicating source noise. No fatalities are recorded in any conflict entry, and there is no corroborating evidence in this window of organized armed violence, insurgent activity, or terrorist attacks on Moroccan soil.
analysis.political_stability_analysis: Civil-unrest signal in this dataset is minimal: only one protest_civil_unrest event is recorded, dated 2026-07-02, and it derives from the same Spain-Morocco counterterrorism cooperation article rather than a distinct domestic protest report. The three political_violence_targeting_civilians entries (2026-06-30, GDELT) similarly reference the UN's feature on Amina Bouayach (a human rights figure) and unrelated US/Mexico stories, not verified attacks on Moroccan civilians. Based strictly on this data window, there is no substantive evidence of domestic political violence or unrest in Morocco; the risk picture is effectively unmeasured rather than confirmed low, given the apparent coding noise.
analysis.trend_summary: Morocco's data profile in this window is dominated by steady macroeconomic indicators (IMF/World Bank) and a large, diverse base of investment/development-finance activity (123 events) spanning World Bank PPI infrastructure projects, Chinese health-sector grants, and smaller US DFC lending. By contrast, the conflict, protest, and political-violence categories contain very few events (9, 1, and 3 respectively) and on close inspection most of these appear to be GDELT coding artifacts tied to diplomatic/cooperation news rather than substantive unrest or violence. This suggests a security and political-stability picture that reads as calm in the available data, though largely because the signal is thin and partly noisy rather than because of strong positive evidence. Economically, growth is robust and stable (4.9% in both 2025 and 2026, IMF) with low inflation, but debt remains elevated (~66-67% of GDP) and the current account deficit is projected to widen in 2026. Investment activity is real and multi-sourced (World Bank PPI private sector, Chinese state financiers, US DFC) but the most recent large-project entries in this dataset date to 2023-2024, with no comparably sized new commitments captured through mid-2026.
